flow: Part 2 个人陈述(准备1分钟,陈述1分30秒)+ 两人讨论(3分钟)

cue.t: Should college students be required to take part in volunteer work?

roles.title: Pair discussion
roles.setting: Many young people now prefer to work in big cities, while others choose to go back to their hometowns. Discuss with your partner the advantages and disadvantages of both choices.
task: Try to come to a conclusion.

steps.t: Good afternoon. Welcome to the CET Spoken English Test. First, please introduce yourself.
What do you usually do to relax after a busy week?
Thank you. Now, Part Two. First, you'll give a presentation. You have one minute to prepare.
Thank you. Now, you'll discuss a topic with your partner.
I think big cities offer more job opportunities and higher salaries. That's why I want to stay in a big city.

steps.cue: 回应对方,并指出大城市的缺点

steps.t: Well, that's a problem. But small towns often don't have the jobs we studied for.

steps.cue: 承认对方的观点,补充回家乡的优点

steps.t: So maybe it depends on the person's career and priorities?
Thank you. Now, Part Three. Do you think the government should do more to help young people find jobs? Why?

model: Good afternoon. I'm Wang Fang, a junior majoring in international trade. I'm interested in cross-cultural communication, and in my spare time I enjoy photography and traveling.
points: 简洁、自然

q1.q: What do you usually do to relax after a busy week?
q1.ja: 忙碌的一周后,你通常怎么放松?
model: I usually go for a long walk in the park or watch a movie with my roommates. It helps me clear my mind and get ready for the next week.
points: 回答 + 理由或例子

pres.q: Should college students be required to take part in volunteer work?
model: In my opinion, volunteer work should be encouraged, but it shouldn't be required. On the one hand, volunteering has many benefits. Students can develop a sense of responsibility and learn skills that they can't learn in the classroom. For example, last year I taught English to children in a rural school for two weeks, and it made me much more patient. On the other hand, if volunteering becomes compulsory, some students may do it only to get credits, without real enthusiasm. That would not help the people they are supposed to serve. So I think universities should offer more opportunities and rewards, but leave the final choice to students.
points: 观点明确
两个理由,各有例子
总结

q3.q: Do you think the government should do more to help young people find jobs? Why?
q3.ja: 你认为政府应该做更多来帮助年轻人就业吗?为什么?
model: Yes, I do. The government could provide more training programs and support for small businesses, which create a lot of jobs. It could also help graduates in rural areas get internships. These measures would reduce unemployment and make society more stable.
points: 深入一点:原因、影响、建议

d1.q: I think big cities offer more job opportunities and higher salaries. That's why I want to stay in a big city.
d1.ja: 回应对方,并指出大城市的缺点
model: That's true, but the cost of living in big cities is very high. Housing alone can take half of a young person's salary.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

d2.q: Well, that's a problem. But small towns often don't have the jobs we studied for.
d2.ja: 承认对方的观点,补充回家乡的优点
model: I agree that's a challenge. However, with remote work, more jobs can be done from anywhere. And in your hometown, you can stay close to your family.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

d3.q: So maybe it depends on the person's career and priorities?
model: Exactly. It depends on the industry and what people value most. Young people should think carefully about their long-term goals before deciding.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

cue.t: Is artificial intelligence a help or a threat to college students?

roles.title: Pair discussion
roles.setting: Some people think university students should live on campus, while others prefer to rent an apartment off campus. Discuss the pros and cons with your partner.

steps.t: Good afternoon. Welcome to the CET Spoken English Test. First, please introduce yourself.
How often do you use social media, and what do you use it for?
Thank you. Now, Part Two. First, you'll give a presentation. You have one minute to prepare.
Thank you. Now, you'll discuss a topic with your partner.
Living on campus is cheaper and more convenient. You can walk to class in five minutes.

steps.cue: 回应,并提出校外住宿的优点

steps.t: True, but living off campus can make you feel isolated from campus life.
So which do you think is better for first-year students?
Thank you. Now, Part Three. How do you think universities can better prepare students for their future careers?

model: Good afternoon. I'm Wang Fang, a junior majoring in international trade. I'm interested in cross-cultural communication, and in my spare time I enjoy photography and traveling.
points: 简洁、自然

q1.q: How often do you use social media, and what do you use it for?
q1.ja: 你多久用一次社交媒体?用来做什么?
model: I use it every day, mainly to keep in touch with my friends and to follow news about technology. I try to limit it to about an hour a day.
points: 回答 + 理由或例子

pres.q: Is artificial intelligence a help or a threat to college students?
model: I believe artificial intelligence is mainly a help to college students, as long as we use it wisely. Today, many students use AI tools to search for information, check their grammar or get explanations of difficult concepts. For instance, when I didn't understand a statistics problem, an AI tool explained it to me step by step, which saved me a lot of time. However, there are also risks. Some students simply copy answers from AI and stop thinking for themselves, and the information AI gives is not always correct. Therefore, students should use AI as a learning partner, not as a replacement for their own work, and always check important facts.
points: 观点明确
两个理由,各有例子
总结

q3.q: How do you think universities can better prepare students for their future careers?
q3.ja: 你认为大学怎样才能更好地帮助学生为将来的职业做准备?
model: Universities could offer more internships and invite professionals to share their experience. They could also teach practical skills like teamwork and communication, not just theory. This would help students move smoothly from campus to the workplace.
points: 深入一点:原因、影响、建议

d1.q: Living on campus is cheaper and more convenient. You can walk to class in five minutes.
d1.ja: 回应,并提出校外住宿的优点
model: That's a good point. But living off campus gives you more privacy and freedom. In a dorm, it's hard to study when your roommates are noisy.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

d2.q: True, but living off campus can make you feel isolated from campus life.
model: I agree. Campus activities are an important part of college. Maybe students who live off campus need to make more effort to join clubs.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去

d3.q: So which do you think is better for first-year students?
model: For first-year students, I think living on campus is better, because it helps them make friends and adapt to college life. Later, they can choose for themselves.
points: 回应对方 → 提出自己的看法
用问题把讨论继续下去
